main_text.p: stes Romanos. Ut verò respirare aliquibus licuit, & feriari, non quiescere, mox totâ mente & studio ad tractandam jucundissimam & saluberrimam Theologiæ partem, quæ in moribus & vitâ ad Reformationem componendâ versatur, impigre se transtulerunt. Quæ præsertim vobis Anglis contigit temporum & rerum felicitas, à gloriss.[?] mem. Reginâ, in exemplum datâ Regum omnium, Principumque, ELISABETA. Unde factum, ut Ecclesiæ Anglicæ in hoc genere doctrinæ supra alias emicuerint, & paucæ idem potuerint, nisi earum exemplum gnaviter æmulari.Neque enim pudet agnoscere[?], quæ divina liberalitas aliis indulsit, præsertim talia, quæ in nostros non minus usus redundant, quam ipsorum. Præter Papismum autem Ecclesiis omnibus pariter infestum, sua singulæ experiuntur mala propria & domestica:

page.notes: The first word "stes" is a fragment from the previous page (Romanos, rest of "Romanos"); the paragraph is carried over from the previous page. Long s and st ligatures are read as s. The mark after "omnium" and the mark after "agnoscere" are small tilde-like signs of uncertain meaning; I have written the words without them. "gloriss." is an abbreviation of uncertain reading. "ELISABETA" is set in small capitals in the print. There is no space after "æmulari." before "Neque", as printed. No page number, catchword or signature is visible.
